title: Extracellular vesicle isolation from bacterial cultures
author: Steven Biller
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8fzhtp6
materials: Grow bacterial culture to mid/late exponential phase

steps.title: Remove cells by filtration
steps.instruction: If needed, centrifuge the bacterial culture at ~10,000 × g (or less) to pellet bulk cells, then filter the supernatant through a Whatman Polycap TC 0.2 µm capsule filter (catalog 6717‑9502) to collect the <0.2 µm filtrate.

steps.title: Concentrate filtrate with TFF
steps.instruction: Concentrate the <0.2 µm, cell‑free supernatant using a tangential flow filtration device equipped with a 100 kDa cutoff membrane, keeping the feed pressure below 10 psi and reducing the volume as much as possible.

steps.title: Re‑filter concentrated material
steps.instruction: Pass the concentrated supernatant through a 0.2 µm syringe filter to remove any remaining large particles.

steps.title: Pellet vesicles by ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Ultracentrifuge the filtered material at 100,000 × g for at least 1 hour at 10 °C or lower to pellet extracellular vesicles.

steps.title: Remove supernatant and optional wash
steps.instruction: Carefully discard as much supernatant as possible; if desired, wash the vesicle pellet with an appropriate buffer (e.g., culture media or 1× PBS) for downstream applications.

steps.title: Resuspend and store vesicles
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final vesicle pellet in the chosen buffer and store at –20 °C or –80 °C.
